SEC-07 access log ↔ SEC-02 attribution: access.open / access.denied entries carry {module, role:currentRole(), admin:isAdmin} plus the auditLog person-actor, so the access log shows the person and the role, not a bare role label.

Restore/backup security contract: PIN + role state + staff-PIN hashes stay in restoreBlockedKeys() (never imported); the attempt/lockout key is BOTH restore-blocked AND out of appControlKeys() (never exported); policy keys (pin_policy, staff_login_required, launch_lock) are exportable and MUST be bounded/clamped by the restore validator.
slicing.deviceRiskGate: All four slices are 'light' on storage (UI/logic only; no storage-core.js/sqlite-store.js/photo-store.js contact — that never-touch rule is NOT lifted for R0-W1). They differ only in device-test dependency, which is what gates ship. Slice A (named identity + JML + access logging) is SAFE to harness-verify and SHIP PRE-DEVICE-TEST: no launch gate, no lockout timer, no money-action block, fail-open by nature, and its one real hazard (unguarded auditLog throw) is fully handled by try/catch — nothing in it can brick. Slices B, C, D MUST pass an on-device test before ship: (B) regress the prompt()-based re-auth on the Android WebView (a PIN-configured owner with a suppressed prompt would be blocked from a money action) — device-test the money-action + export flow; (C) device-test the three lockout paths — correct unlock still works, N-wrong then temporary lock that AUTO-EXPIRES, no-PIN onboarding never locks — because time is the only non-destructive recovery on a packaged APK; (D) is the R0 GO/NO-GO — never validated on harness alone, requiring on-device confirmation that the DOM overlay captures focus/keyboard, hardware-back is intercepted while locked, and a no-PIN device opens straight through. Recommended cadence: ship A on harness; hold B/C/D for the per-slice device-test, with D as the hard R0 sign-off gate.
newKeysConsolidated: SHIPPING — st_v2_pin_policy_v1 (SEC-03, Slice C): configurable policy {minLen:4, maxFails:5, baseLockSec:30, maxLockSec:300, rejectTrivial:false, forceChangeAdmin:false, forceChangeStaff:{}}. Placement: appControlKeys() (exportable) + APP_RE (auto-covered by st_v\d+_) + a BOUNDED validateRestoreKeyValue() 'control' branch that clamps minLen (e.g. 4..12) and coerces numerics. NOT restoreBlockedKeys — config, not secret.

SHIPPING — st_v2_pin_attempts_v1 (SEC-03, Slice C): device-local lockout state {admin:{fails,lockUntil,lastFailAt}, staff:{<empId>:{...}}}. Placement: APP_RE (factory-reset clears it) + restoreBlockedKeys() (never imported). DELIBERATELY NOT in appControlKeys() (never exported) — closes lockout-injection/DoS. Bends the 'all new keys → appControlKeys' rule; needs owner/orchestrator sign-off.

SHIPPING — saagar_staff_login_required_v1 (SEC-02, Slice A): owner policy, require a per-staff PIN before a staffer can be signed in for attribution. DEFAULT ABSENT/OFF = current fail-open. Placement: appControlKeys() + EXPLICIT APP_RE inclusion (the saagar_ prefix is NOT matched by APP_RE's st_v\d+_ pattern) + validateRestoreKeyValue() 'control' branch. NOT restoreBlockedKeys (policy, not secret; mirrors ROLE_SWITCH_LOCK_KEY).

SHIPPING (opt-in) — st_v2_launch_lock (P1-37, Slice D): boolean, DEFAULT ABSENT/OFF; effective gate = hasAdminPin() && launchLockEnabled(). Placement: appControlKeys() + APP_RE (auto st_v\d+_) + validateRestoreKeyValue() 'control' branch accepting the boolean. NOT restoreBlockedKeys — the hasAdminPin() AND-guard makes it fail-open on a device whose PIN was restore-blocked.
OMITTED for R0-W1 (decided against; hard-code always-on-when-PIN): st_v2_sensitive_reauth (SEC-04) and st_v2_money_reauth (P1-51). Fewer keys, no restore rules, still fail-open.
NO new key — SEC-05 (JML) reuses EMP_MASTER_KEY/STAFF_PIN_KEY/ACTIVE_STAFF_KEY; SEC-07 reuses AUDIT_LOG_KEY + ui_hide_amounts.
openQuestionsForOwner: Enforcement default for NEW installs: should staff-login-required (SEC-02) and/or launch-lock (P1-37) default ON for fresh installs while staying OFF for existing devices (a first-run-vs-upgrade split), or is opt-in-OFF-everywhere acceptable to the auditor for R0-W1?

Confirm the deliberate rule-bend: st_v2_pin_attempts_v1 kept OUT of appControlKeys() (never exported) to prevent lockout-injection/DoS — sign-off needed since it deviates from the 'all new keys → appControlKeys' hard rule.
SEC-03 lockout parameters: confirm maxLockSec cap (recommend ≤5 min, the only non-destructive on-APK recovery is auto-expiry), the escalation ladder (e.g. 30s/1m/2m/5m), and maxFails (recommend 5).

SEC-07 SENSITIVE_VIEWS membership for access-logging: is ['payroll','tax'] enough, or must 'expense' (cash), 'dsr' (cash sales) and 'cro_audit' (full customer list) also be logged? Full-module logging risks flooding the 500-entry ring — recommend sensitive-only.

P1-51 exact money-action site list: confirm the ~14 functions (payroll setRunStatus/lockRun/unlockRun/closeMonth; expense finishClose/voidEntry/approveDay/reopenDay/monthlock; stock toggleLock/doLockClosing/submitMovements/doReopenConfirm; dsr submitAudit/unlockForCorrection) — include or exclude dsr submitDay?

Does 'every login maps to a named employee' (SEC-02/SEC-05 bar) accept the named OWNER via OWNER_NAME_KEY, given the owner is deliberately NOT an employee row? (We must NOT create an owner employee row.)
P1-37 named-access scope: owner-PIN-only launch (recommended MVP), or should launch also accept any valid STAFF PIN and auto-sign-in that staffer for attribution?
SEC-05 offboarding: should Archive ALWAYS auto-clear the staff PIN (true revocation, recommended) while plain Deactivate keeps it for easy reactivation?
SEC-03 trivial-PIN rejection (0000/1234/1111): include as an opt-in flag (default off) or skip for R0-W1?
Confirm deep in-iframe salary-column masking is deferred (touches module blobs = heavier than 'light'); role-scoping already blocks the module for unauthorized roles.
slicing.recommendedFirst: Slice A — Named identity + JML enforcement + access logging (SEC-02 + SEC-05 + SEC-07). Lowest-brick-risk, highest-value: pure logic plus guarded logging plus one default-OFF policy key, with no launch gate, no lockout timer, and no money-action block — nothing in it can lock the owner out, and it is fail-open by construction. It establishes the two contracts every later slice consumes (the named-identity source of truth for attribution/JML, and access logging), and it is the only slice safe to ship on harness verification ahead of the device-test queue. The single must-do hazard is wrapping every new auditLog call in try/catch so the access-logging instrumentation in openModule/ensureModuleAccess cannot throw and brick module access.
